speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand what might be causing these skin lesions, can you tell me how long they have been present and if they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Can you describe the appearance of the papules, such as their color and whether they have a central dimple or crust? Also, has the child had any fever or other systemic symptoms recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication is classic for molluscum contagiosum. Given the history of daycare exposure and typical lesion appearance, I am confident in this assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
